dct_description_sm: The main purpose of the Beaufort Sea Regional Environmental Assessment - Marine Fishes Project (BREA-MFP) was to assess baseline characteristics (i.e., the diversity, distributions, relative abundances, and basic biological parameters) of offshore marine fishes in the Canadian Beaufort Sea in order to inform future regulatory processes pertaining to oil and gas development in the region.   The specific objectives of this work were to 1) establish regional baseline information on fish occurrences and diversity, 2) determine fish community structure and habitat associations, and 3) to establish the functional relationships within and among deepwater slope, shelf and coastal benthic and pelagic sub-ecosystems (e.g., couplings associated with differential habitat use over the life histories of key fish species; diet, productivity and energetic linkages derived from stable isotope and fatty acid analyses; and baselines for key indicator contaminants).   The baseline information contained in this dataset can be used to predict and assess the impacts of future oil and gas development and climate change and will support the development of regulatory frameworks (e.g. through identification of critical habitats), project planning and future conservation and monitoring efforts.  This dataset contains fishing net deployment data and basic biological information for fish caught during the 2012 BREA expedition.
dct_title_s: Beaufort Regional Environmental Assessment (BREA) Marine Fishes Project - Distribution and Abundance of Offshore Marine fishes in the Canadian Beaufort Sea, Summer 2012
